lookback_notes: NOT_FOUND. The audit criteria for Area 29 (Incorrect PRI Level Claimed) on p. 18 state no observation/look-back window; they only state that the PRI Level must be supported by the record. A 7-day window appears on the same page but belongs to a different finding area (Area 30, 'Patient Review Instrument Invalid Resident not on site for the look back period': 'dated while the patient is not in the facility on that date or the 7 days prior'), and is not stated as applying to Area 29. No window is therefore recorded for this item.

federal.notes: Framed as the OMIG Audit Criteria for this finding area; non-support of the level drives a payment-difference disallowance.

state_deltas.delta: This is a New York State OMIG audit protocol; Area 29 (Incorrect PRI Level Claimed) applies to ALP claims with service dates on or after 01/01/2013 and prior to 03/01/2015, per the page header and the phase-out note.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The document ties the PRI Level directly to the amount payable: an unsupported level results in re-determination of the correct level and disallowance of the difference between the appropriate and paid claim amounts. Regulatory references include the rate-setting provision 10 NYCRR § 86-2.30(a) and (c).

conflicts.topic: Service-date range applicable to this finding area

positions.claim: The protocol as a whole covers service dates 01/01/2013 through 10/31/2025.
The page containing Area 29 is scoped to service dates 01/01/2013 through 02/28/2015.

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: the heading 'For Services Dates Prior to 03/01/2015' on p. 17 limits findings 25-30 (including Area 29) to service dates before 03/01/2015, while the overall protocol covers 01/01/2013 through 10/31/2025.
